intro: Step onto the Adana Stone Bridge, in Adana province, a Roman bridge of the 4th century AD over the Seyhan. It has been in continuous use for seventeen centuries, and it carried motor traffic until 2007.
history: The bridge over the Seyhan was built in the fourth century AD, and it has been in use ever since. Fourteen of its original twenty-one arches survive. It was repaired several times under the Ottomans, carried motor traffic until 2007, and today it belongs to pedestrians — to you.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman arches and their cutwaters, then look for the traces of Ottoman repair, and finally the bridgehead.
facts: Did you know? It is among the oldest bridges anywhere still in use, having carried everything from ox carts to lorries across seventeen centuries. This Roman bridge carried motor traffic right up until 2007. And fourteen of its original twenty-one arches still survive.
outro: This brings our journey across the Adana Stone Bridge to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Countless feet have crossed here before yours; may many more cross after you. Enjoy your visit.
